page.layout: One block of running text in one column; running head centred above the text; page number at the top left; a catchword-like word "lam" at the lower right below the last line. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: losophorum, postquam in praelaris, quos de Moribus inscripsit libris, virum optimum formauit ac instituit, parum praestitisse se existimauit, nisi ciuem quoque optimum ac ciuitatis principem formaret. Quippe quod à summo maximoque praeceptore suo factum meminisset. qui cum in Lachete, de fortitudine, in Charmide de temperantia, in Lyside de amicitia, in Philebo de voluptate, in Menone de virtute tota, qua verborum est foecunditate ac inuentionum, more illo suo, qui ab Aristotelis docendi ac dicendi ratione quantum dici poteft alienus ac diuersus est, fusissime egisset, tandem de Rep. & ciuitate tota libris decem eleganter ac prolixe disputauit. Quibus & duodecim De legibus, De summo ciuitatis hominisque bono vnum, qui Epinomis inscribitur, subjunxit. Mihi vero sic videtur: hoc, vt alia non pauca, vnius Dei beneficium ac donum esse, quod, vt omnes quae singulos perficiunt virtutes, ita optimum totius ciuitatis constituendae ac formandae modum, a duobus summis sapientiae magistris, cum quibus quod componat neque aetas nostra neque tota habuit antiquitas, tradi ac exponi voluerit. Quare qui doceri hanc scientiam non posse existimat, quid & quantum in his vterque libris praestiterit, non satis animum aduertit. Nam qui nihil praeter vmbraticos fuisse doctores, nullam

page.notes: Page header reads "318" and "DANIELIS HEINSII". The first line "losophorum" is a continuation of "Philosophorum" from the previous page, rendered as printed. The word "lam" at the lower right is the catchword, and it is also the start of the last line's continuation; it is kept as the catchword only. Some long s rendered as s; "Quippe quod" and "Quibus" have underlined Q as printed. Doubtful readings: "quod componat" and "fingulos" appear as printed.
